facts.fact: A jogini lakeside cairn stands on a shelf above the shore of the Mirror, 910 of Ila's paces from the foot of the Widow's Ladder. Its hum rises when a lie is begun near it and settles at a true word.
facts.why: needed because the beat places the near-kiss at a lakeside cairn whose hum interrupts Kunal's lie (extends F320).

facts.fact: Kunal's fingertips go numb and wax-pale briefly when he begins the lie 'It doesn't matter to me what you d--' and stops; the cold fades after he speaks the truth, leaving an ache.
facts.why: shows the rule biting on an unfinished lie without a full lie-cost.

facts.fact: Ila sounds ice by tapping an axe haft: clear ice rings, rotten ice goes dull.
facts.why: needed because the beat has her wanting to sound the Mirror before crossing.

facts.fact: Kunal's uncle Pritam taught him 'Whoever knows the way owns the people, Kunal. Remember it. Everything else is manners.' over supper when Kunal was young.
facts.why: gives the outline's uncle's-lesson beat a concrete wording.
